source.public_versification_note: All 618 Judges public references align one to one with source records; this pass reread 265 selected records.

chapter_reading_record.observations: Judah/Simeon brother language, capture versus failed expulsion, forced labor, Kenite kinship, Othniel/Achsah and the Dan restriction remain coherent without harmonizing Joshua.
The return to Joshua’s lifetime is clear. Covenant, abandonment, judges, rescue, hand, groaning, corruption and testing establish the recurring cycle.
Asheroth remains distinct from Ashtaroth. Exact service/rest counts, Ehud’s left hand and right thigh, difficult bodily/architectural phrases and Shamgar’s separate notice remain.

Deborah’s female prophetic and judging role, Barak’s conditional reply, the woman’s hand, chariot count and Jael’s killing retain their specific agents. This prose account is not merged with the song.

The complete song retains parallel lines, repetitions, changing speakers, communal participation, difficult old wording and the captive-women image. Two lines refined for degree and chariot sound, with the footsteps image noted.

Gideon’s accusation remains his voice, grasp renders kaph while hand commonly renders yad, the two-bull ambiguity remains noted, the Spirit clothing image survives, and opposite fleece tests remain distinct.
Gilead, drinking descriptions, camp geography, 22,000/10,000/300 counts and distinct instructions/performed battle cries remain; pursuit is not harmonized with the next chapter’s crossing.

Ephraim’s gleanings, captured-hands threat, violence at Succoth/Penuel, counts, rule refusal, ephod/snare and household kindness remain visible. Abimelech’s birth and kingly name are not flattened into an explanation.

The tree fable remains connected prose with repeated invitations, sway, shade and reciprocal fire. Seventy sons and surviving Jotham, slave-woman speech, evil spirit, shifting companies and the unnamed woman remain.
All minor-judge family/town/year counts, foreign gods, Maon and repeated abandonment/rescue terms remain. That year and eighteen years are retained together.
Commander/head negotiation, rival land account, Chemosh, 300 years and the LORD as Judge remain. Spirit and vow remain separate; the unnamed daughter’s loss and restrained fulfillment are preserved.
Ephraim’s second confrontation differs from Gideon’s earlier response. The fugitives taunt, Shibboleth test, 42,000 deaths and minor-judge notices remain without normalization.
The woman’s encounters, distinct announcement and retelling, womb consecration, begin rescue, wonder/name relation and wife’s reasoning remain clear.
Right in my eyes connects to the book’s refrain. The riddle, heifer image, seven/three-day tension and killings retain separate speakers and literary forms.
Reciprocal retaliation, the woman and father’s deaths, numerical details, jawbone poem, Lehi spring and twenty years under Philistine power remain.
Full-heart disclosure now reads naturally in all three occurrences across 17–18. Loom gap, affliction, mutilation, rooftop count, revenge ambiguity and death comparison remain.
Micah’s dedication/image contradiction, 1,100/200/10 silver figures, father/son/priest relations and exact closing-book refrain remain.
Dan’s inheritance claim, oracle, uncertain Laish clause, distinct object lists, violence against a quiet secure people, Manasseh/Moses issue and Shiloh/exile notices remain.

Corrected the father’s plural stay command and clarified the husband’s agency. All time markers, uncertain departure/destination readings, sexual violence, master designation, threshold image and unannounced time of death remain.

The Levite’s account remains distinct from the narrator. The opening Judah-first question echoes 1:1, now against Benjamin. All inquiries, retrospective battle scenes, disputed place forms and nonmatching casualty totals remain.
The two human oaths, killing and captive-taking, Shiloh abduction, inheritance language and exact 17:6 refrain remain. The elders’ uncertain oath argument remains qualified rather than endorsed.

cross_book_themes.decision: Preserve evil in the LORD’s eyes, Samson’s right-in-eyes claims, the host’s good-in-eyes offer and the final exact refrain. Moral speakers remain distinguishable.
Retain meaningful bodily power imagery; grasp in 6:13–14 reflects kaph and does not require mechanical harmonization to hand.
Preserve came upon, clothed himself, began to stir, rushed upon, and left according to their verbs. Do not turn the following actions or human vows into divine commands.
Retain each period as stated, including repeated twenty-year Samson notices; do not sum them into an unsupported linear chronology.
Preserve specific gender, distinct narratorial and quoted designations, naming or anonymity, and explicit harm. Clarify the husband’s action at 19:25 without changing master in 26–27.
Retain inheritance and tribe/clan distinctions while recording Dan’s allotment tension. No book-to-book historical harmonization.
Keep Ashtaroth/Asheroth/Asherah, Baal-berith/El-berith and the object lists distinct. Vocabulary explains terms without claiming an exact ephod reconstruction.
Preserve narrative and poetic differences, the woman’s retelling, temporal tensions, the Levite’s omitted action and the retrospective battle account. Do not make repeated accounts identical.

source_detail: All 265 selected original XML records were read, including their written/read and other annotations, and bound by exact substring hash. The pinned morphology identifies 19:8 vehitmahmehu as a plural imperative (HC/Vtv2mp).
comparator_review: The five changed verses were compared with TSW after source-led refinement. Earlier complete TSW comparisons remain documented in the original batches. No additional full-book TSW rereading is claimed for this pass.
overlap_qualification: Existing revised draft comparison only; similarity is not proof of originality, fidelity or comprehension.
preserved_provenance: Original source, base commits, initial before text, comparators and editorial classifications remain in the ledgers. Five refinements have additive history. Two affected ledgers and three chapter bindings are rebound; historical reports remain snapshots.
review_limits: This is a translation-authoring self-check, not an independent Hebrew review or publication approval.
The entire English draft and apparatus were read; this pass reread 265 selected Hebrew verses, not every Hebrew verse anew. Complete first-source readings were recorded in the three draft batches.

Consequential uncertainties remain in chapter 5’s old poetry, 6:25–26, 7:3–8, 9:31,44, 11:24,31,37–40, 14:4,15, 16:13–14,28, 17:3–4,7, 18:7,18,30, 19:2,18, 20:31–43,48 and 21:22. Existing notes preserve alternatives.
No reader-comprehension or listening test has occurred.
